overview: Recognize shingle types and materials quickly. Compare Architectural vs. 3‑Tab, understand discontinued considerations, and practice manufacturer identification tips.
learningObjectives: Explain English vs. Metric dimensions and exposure

sections.title: Architectural vs. 3‑Tab
sections.content: Architectural (dimensional/laminated): multi‑layer, textured appearance, varied shadow lines, better longevity. 3‑Tab (strip): single layer, uniform tabs, straight lines, shorter lifespan. Many 3‑Tab lines are discontinued or phasing out, which often triggers matching arguments.

sections.title: English vs. Metric Dimensions
sections.content: English and Metric shingles have different exposure sizes. Mixing causes misalignment and prevents proper sealing. Repairs with incompatible dimensions result in visual mismatch — a common basis for full replacement.

sections.title: Discontinued Signals
sections.content: Older 3‑Tab lines (e.g., Royal Sovereign, XT 25, Supreme) and architectural lines 15+ years old are frequently discontinued. Verify via manufacturer sites and iTel. Use Module 13 for templates and code support.

sections.title: Manufacturer Identification Tips
sections.content: Check shingle backs for stamps, compare granule tone and cut pattern, review homeowner documentation, and reference photo guides. Practice until you can ID common lines at a glance.
